to Nouvelle-France, 1842-1958
The early history of the city of Tours is closely related to that of the capital of France. The Tours of the Middle Ages was a major trading port in the medieval period and it was also a port of entry for the French kings. The city grew around the town walls, which were constructed during the reigns of Louis VI, Louis VII and Louis VIII.
The first phase of Tours' development was as a commercial center of France. It developed into an important trading center in the 10th century, when it became the most powerful city in the region. The city became a major centre of culture and commerce in the Middle Ages. In the 11th century, Tours became a capital of the Kingdom of France and during the reigns of Louis VII and Louis VIII it became a major port city.
Tours' growth was interrupted by the French Revolution, but the city was revived as a center of culture and commerce after World War II. The city is still one of the most important centres in France and is one of the best examples of a Renaissance town. It has become a popular tourist destination with its rich medieval history.
